# tidewatch

> A tiny command-line tool that tells you when the tide will be high enough to launch a boat.

[![build](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-brightgreen)](#) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

`tidewatch` reads tide predictions for a harbour, compares them with the draft of your boat, and prints the windows in which you can safely leave or return. It has no account system, no telemetry and one dependency.

## Table of contents

- [Installation](#installation)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Contributing](#contributing)

## Installation

```bash
# with npm
npm install --global tidewatch

# or run it once without installing
npx tidewatch --harbour "St Ives" --draft 1.2
```

Node.js **18 or newer** is required. On Windows, use PowerShell or WSL; the classic `cmd.exe` prompt does not render the table correctly.

## Quick start

```bash
tidewatch --harbour "St Ives" --draft 1.2 --days 3
```

Example output:

| Day       | Window        | Min depth | Notes            |
|-----------|---------------|-----------|------------------|
| Fri 14    | 05:10 – 08:45 | 1.9 m     |                  |
| Fri 14    | 17:30 – 21:05 | 2.1 m     | sunset at 20:41  |
| Sat 15    | 06:00 – 09:30 | 1.8 m     | spring tide      |

Times are local to the harbour. A window is only shown when the predicted depth stays above `draft + margin` for at least 30 minutes.

## Configuration

Settings can be passed as flags or stored in `~/.config/tidewatch/config.toml`:

```toml
harbour = "St Ives"
draft   = 1.2      # metres
margin  = 0.4      # extra water under the keel
units   = "metric" # or "imperial"
```

| Flag         | Default  | Description                                   |
|--------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `--harbour`  | *(none)* | Harbour name or station id                    |
| `--draft`    | `1.0`    | Draft of the boat in metres                   |
| `--margin`   | `0.3`    | Safety margin added to the draft              |
| `--days`     | `2`      | How many days to look ahead (max 14)          |
| `--json`     | `false`  | Print machine-readable output instead         |

## FAQ

**Is this safe to rely on?**
No. Predictions ignore wind, pressure and river flow, all of which can move the real water level by half a metre or more. Treat the output as a starting point and *always* check the official tables and the sky.

**Why is my harbour missing?**
The bundled list covers about 400 stations. You can add your own with `tidewatch stations add <file.csv>`; see [docs/stations.md](docs/stations.md) for the format.

**Can it send me a reminder?**
Not directly, but `--json` output is easy to pipe into `cron`, `ntfy` or a home-automation system.

## Contributing

1. Fork the repository and create a branch: `git checkout -b fix/my-change`
2. Run the tests with `npm test`
3. Open a pull request and describe *why* the change is needed

Bug reports are welcome. Please include the command you ran, the output, and your operating system.
